title: Derive two-write spectator constraints with exact middle-label projection
body:
PR6012 leaves a two-write spectator lemma open in its residual five-coordinate, ten-call two-cycle problem. This package derives the exact row-stabilizer projection while retaining the middle labels selected by `e_j^T b=e_l^T` and their required relabelling `g b h`.

For an endpoint `[c]I` in the two-role binary formal model, a coordinate written exactly twice has **equal** rank-one scalar projectors when `c` restores that row, and **complementary** projectors when `c` moves it. The moved-row result uses the projections of both the word and its inverse; the forward equation alone admits additional pairs. In PR6012's residual `(6,4)` case, these restrictions apply to both writer and reader pairs.

A standard five-call commutator gives an exact identity with a spectator written and read twice. It disproves an unrestricted three-write spectator rule; inserting it before the known twelve-call endpoint supplies a seventeen-call positive control. It is not a ten-call counterexample. The full length-ten and length-eleven exclusions remain open.

Validation passes on exact head `188cee674895aa8c1e63aafa91003e34c237e420`: normal and optimized registered checks; 3,600 formal projection contexts; all 576 augmented matrix cases; six commutator identities; a separate complete-permutation group-label engine checking 288 return filters, 72 outer contexts and six seventeen-call endpoints; source pins/history and committed bytes; official export integrity; and read-only Git-free empty-PATH replays with source mutation rejection. A separate read-only agent reviewed the algebra and independently checked the matrix and group fixtures. This is not independent human or proof-kernel acceptance.

Reproduce with `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/two-write-spectator-projection`.

Credit Nick Petalas/#6012 for the projection/reduction question, Mihir Srivastava/#4939 for the formal model, James Reed/jwr404 #5005/#5379 for the cited small-dimension results, and JoyboyBrian/#4974 for the earlier single-cycle reduction. The commutator is standard. Prepared by JoyboyBrian with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. [Advance claim and canonical discussion](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/6075).

No native supplier, tariff, selected-frontier change or new kappa is claimed. Hosted CI has not yet completed. The canonical base currently fails two current-status navigation tests before scientific replay; existing PR #6050 repairs those documentation mismatches. Local validation above is separate from hosted CI.
